pages.text: We are in a rift created between the realms of dead and living. I am the one who first had the dreams that now haunt the young boy in Abel. I was keeping a record of those dreams, but when I finally understood it - when the words of the gods became clear - I could not handle it.

pages.name: Dreamer
pages.text: It was a long story, I will try to make it short. One day, a tragic accident happened, and a young girl nearly lost her life. She was saved by a poor man, but that act cost him his own health. Seeing that, Danaan rewarded him with a cap. When he wore it, he became healthier again. That was the Cap of Danaan.

pages.name: Dreamer
pages.text: The other deities offered to make the cap more powerful, but the man declined, being alive and healthy was enough for him.

pages.name: Dreamer

choices.text: What happened to the Cap of Danaan?

pages.name: Dreamer
pages.text: It is said Fiosachd hid it, so no one unworthy would wear it. After Danaan's sacrifice, however, the gods wished to hand it to their fighters, the Aislings, to aid in their battle. They would keep the original, of course, but grant the Aislings Caps of equal power.

pages.name: Dreamer
pages.text: The same offer they made to the poor man, will be offered to the Aislings, each deity can add different powers to the Cap.

choices.text: But these caps were never seen!

Observations.Purpose: Dreamer informational choice: But these caps were never seen!

Arguments.text: But these caps were never seen!

pages.name: Dreamer

choices.text: But these caps were never seen!

pages.name: Dreamer
pages.text: That is true. Four gods - Fiosachd, Gramail, Deoch and Sgrios - did not want to simply hand them freely to the Aislings. They wanted proof of their loyalty to Light.

pages.name: Dreamer
pages.text: So the Caps were withheld until they had such proof.

Observations.Purpose: Dreamer informational choice: There is such proof now?

Arguments.expectedPageText: So the Caps were withheld until they had such proof.

pages.name: Dreamer
pages.text: So the Caps were withheld until they had such proof.

pages.name: Dreamer
pages.text: Yes. The victory of the Champion and Diciples of Light over their Dark counterparts was that proof. The gods then agreed to give the Aislings the Caps.

pages.name: Dreamer
pages.text: But something unexpected happened, and they were delayed.

Observations.Purpose: Dreamer informational choice: What happened?

Arguments.expectedPageText: But something unexpected happened, and they were delayed.

pages.name: Dreamer
pages.text: But something unexpected happened, and they were delayed.

pages.name: Dreamer
pages.text: It is not known how, but the original Cap of Danaan disappeared from its hiding place. This greatly distressed the gods, and they decided to find a better place to hide it, but under more subtle methods.

pages.name: Dreamer
pages.text: A vision from the Acolyte of Gramail, the honor of some Lourian soldiers, the ability of some sneaky thief and his bad luck as he went through the swamp, the "live for the moment" philosophy of a beggar, the love of an arena guard, the endurance of a trapped lady.

pages.name: Dreamer
pages.text: And the original Cap of Danaan is safe again.

choices.text: And why did the boy have those dreams?

Observations.Purpose: Dreamer informational choice: And why did the boy have those dreams?

Arguments.text: And why did the boy have those dreams?
Arguments.expectedPageText: And the original Cap of Danaan is safe again.

pages.name: Dreamer
pages.text: And the original Cap of Danaan is safe again.

choices.text: And why did the boy have those dreams?

pages.name: Dreamer
pages.text: For two reasons. First, because some of the things gods do cannot be explained by each Acolyte in separate, that is why they try to speak to mortals in their dreams.

pages.name: Dreamer
pages.text: And second, because they finally decided to hand Aislings the Caps, and needed a...lure.

Observations.Purpose: Dreamer informational choice: A lure?

Arguments.expectedPageText: And second, because they finally decided to hand Aislings the Caps, and needed a...lure.

pages.name: Dreamer
pages.text: And second, because they finally decided to hand Aislings the Caps, and needed a...lure.

pages.name: Dreamer
pages.text: Yes. This gigantic ordeal you went through, this was part of your test, to know if you are worthy of the Cap of Danaan. It is not the most powerful of items, but it was conceived from the Light of Danaan itself. The gods needed to be sure no one unworthy would wear it. So far, you have proven your worth.

pages.name: Dreamer
pages.text: But one more task is ahead of you.

Observations.Purpose: Dreamer informational choice: It is still not over!?

Arguments.expectedPageText: But one more task is ahead of you.

pages.name: Dreamer
pages.text: But one more task is ahead of you.

pages.name: Dreamer
pages.text: No, There is one more thing for you to do, you must match the poor man's goodness to receive equal benefit. Seek the Avatar father or the son,  either will guide you through the last step. That is all.

pages.name: Dreamer
pages.text: Oh, you must be curious why the gods decided to let the girl in Loures keep the Cap. Well... The young girl saved by the poor man, long ago, she grew up lovely and had a daughter, whom she named Blanchefleur.

pages.name: Dreamer
pages.text: Goodbye.

Observations.Purpose: Dreamer informational choice: Wait, I have more questions!

Arguments.expectedPageText: Goodbye.
